title: Cohomology and linear duals for finite-rank lisse adic coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a separated noetherian scheme of finite dimension on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and use exactly the adic common-stage category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], whose finite-field stages are the raw rationalizations of the derived-complete categories with uniform normalized reduction towers and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Tensor products and internal Homs mean the completed integral operations, their rationalizations, and their common-stage extensions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; they are not operations on discrete non-torsion coefficient sheaves on the small etale site. Let $\mathcal L$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf of finite rank in the adic sense of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], placed in degree zero. Ranks may vary between components and may be zero.

For every $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, the object $K\otimes^L\mathcal L$ belongs to the same $D^b_c$. For every integer $a$, there is a natural isomorphism of adic constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]
$$\mathcal H^a(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)\cong\mathcal H^a(K)\otimes\mathcal L.$$
At every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the induced isomorphism on geometric fibres is
$$\mathcal H^a(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal H^a(K)_{\bar x}\otimes_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}\mathcal L_{\bar x}.$$
Here adic cohomology and its geometric fibres are formed at a common finite coefficient field and then extended to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; on a lisse sheaf this is the fibre of [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors]. These identifications are independent of the chosen common finite field and commute with finite coefficient extension.

The linear dual $\mathcal L^\vee$ is a lisse adic sheaf of finite rank in degree zero, with fibre $(\mathcal L^\vee)_{\bar x}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}(\mathcal L_{\bar x},\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. Its degree-zero realization is isomorphic to the coefficient derived internal dual $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal L,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X})$, where the second argument is the adic coefficient unit. The identifications commute with finite coefficient extension.

external.place: First sentence (exact lisse tensor and geometric fibres), and second sentence (lisse linear dual).

proof.text: Choose a common finite coefficient field $E$ for $K$ and $\mathcal L$, as allowed by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and an integral representative $K_A$, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, $A_n=A/\varpi^n$. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open], $X$ is a finite disjoint union of open connected components. On each nonempty component choose a geometric point. Clause 2 of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] identifies the lisse $E$-sheaf with a continuous finite-dimensional representation of its profinite fundamental group. Apply [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] to choose an invariant finite-free $A$-lattice. Clause 1 of the representation equivalence makes its quotients into finite locally free etale $A_n$-sheaves $L_n$; their quotient maps give $L_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong L_n$. These systems on disjoint open components form one system on $X$. Its rationalization is isomorphic to the original lisse $E$-sheaf by clause 2 of the equivalence. Ranks are bounded because there are finitely many components; rank zero gives the zero system. No assertion that every pro-etale lisse $E_X$-module has a global lisse lattice is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4); integral-lattice argument also in Stanford L19, Proposition 1.1.9, second and third bullets.

proof.text: Put $B=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$. By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], $N=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*L_n$ is pro-etale locally finite free over $B$, and $N/\varpi^nN=\nu_X^*L_n$, naturally with their transitions. Clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], applied to the single stratum $X$ and the local complexes $A^r[0]$, puts $N[0]$ in the exact completed integral category required here, including uniform reduction bounds and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Thus $QN$ realizes $\mathcal L$ at stage $E$. To use the generic tensor/limit result below, identify its coefficient ring $R_X=p_X^*\underline A$ with this $B$ by clause 3 of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. This is a specified ring-sheaf isomorphism, not an identification with the discrete constant sheaf $A_X$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4); integral-category membership by the cited stratified-perfect characterization.

proof.text: Tensoring $B$-module sheaves with $N$ is exact. Indeed restriction to any slice of a trivializing pro-etale covering is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and tensor restricts by [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. There $N=B^r$, so tensor is a finite direct sum of the identity and carries each short exact sequence to its direct sum. The kernel and cokernel of any claimed exactness comparison vanish on this cover; every local section is therefore locally zero and hence zero by the sheaf axiom. This also proves exactness for $r=0$. Consequently, on arbitrary complexes, tensor with $N[0]$ preserves acyclicity: kernels, images and their quotient commute with this exact additive functor. Thus $N[0]$ is K-flat and the ordinary derived tensor $T=K_A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N$ is computed by termwise tensor of any representative $C^\bullet$ of $K_A$.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3; finite-free local calculation of the tensor operation in Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text:
The same kernel/image calculation gives a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^a(T)\cong\mathcal H^a(K_A)\otimes_BN.$$
More explicitly, tensoring the two exact sequences defining the cycles, boundaries and their quotient identifies $Z^a(C\otimes N)$ with $Z^a(C)\otimes N$, and the image of $d^{a-1}\otimes1$ with $\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})\otimes N$; quotienting gives the displayed map. This uses the cohomology convention of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. It is unchanged under a quasi-isomorphism of representatives, since both sides send such a map to an isomorphism, and it is natural in maps of $K_A$ and $N$. The bounded cohomology range is unchanged. By clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], the cohomology of $K_A$ has finite constant local models on finite strata. On a common refinement of their trivializing covers with a cover for $N$, its tensor has the model $(B\otimes_A M)^{\oplus r}=B\otimes_A M^{\oplus r}$, with $M^{\oplus r}$ finitely presented. The same characterization therefore puts $T$ in the required integral category.

source.place: Definition 6.8.8 and Remark 6.8.15; explicit cycles-and-boundaries computation; compatible integral witnesses via the cited characterization.

proof.text:
We now identify this ordinary tensor with the specified completed operation. Apply only the final, generic assertion of [det-lem-int-tensor-product], which allows an arbitrary scheme $S$, to $S=X$ and $M=N$: its local model is the bounded finite-free complex $A^r[0]$. This assertion says that $N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-$ preserves sequential derived inverse limits. Since $K_A$ is complete, [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies its canonical quotient map with $K_A\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n K_n$, where $K_n=K_A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(A_n)_X$. At each level there is the balancing identification
$$N\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_nK_n\cong\operatorname{Res}_n\bigl(K_n\otimes_{(A_n)_X}^{\mathbf L}(N/\varpi^nN)\bigr).$$
On a K-flat representative its map is $y\otimes(x\otimes a)\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes\bar y$, with the usual degree-zero symmetry; the inverse is balancing in the other order. Both maps commute with quotient transitions, because reducing $a$ and $y$ before or after this formula gives the same tensor. Taking $R\varprojlim$ and using limit preservation identifies $T$ with precisely the completed tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The comparisons are natural, including in $N$, because the product/limit comparison is canonical and the levelwise maps are balanced tensor maps. The finite-type characteristic-$p$ tensor-closure assertion earlier in the cited node is not applied.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; completed-tensor comparison using the generic dualizable-factor assertion of blueprint det-lem-int-tensor-product, proof first paragraph.

proof.text:
Rationalize the integral comparison and the cohomology isomorphism. By [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], $Q$ is t-exact and $\mathcal H^a(QK_A)=Q\mathcal H^a(K_A)$, with cohomology computed by integral truncations. Thus the preceding steps give $Q(K_A\widehat\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and
$$\mathcal H^a(QK_A\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}QN)\cong Q(\mathcal H^a(K_A)\otimes_BN).$$
The sheaf tensor on the right is the degree-zero tensor with $QN$: the integral exactness calculation shows that the tensor of any integral heart object with $N$ is concentrated in degree zero, so its rationalized value lies in the rational heart. This explains the cohomology sheaves in the statement as rational cohomology objects, rather than assigning the unlocalized ambient cohomology sheaf to an arbitrary rational representative. All maps extend to rational morphisms: for $f/\varpi^u$ and $g/\varpi^v$, the integral naturality square is multiplied by $\varpi^{-(u+v)}$, as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); localized t-structure interpreted by the cited proposition, followed by rationalizing the integral exact-tensor calculation.

proof.text: To compute fibres, restrict to a lisse stratum for $F=\mathcal H^a(K_A)$; such strata and finite $A$-module local models exist by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. The sheaf quotients $F/\varpi^nF$ have finite constant models on the stratum. Apply [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] to descend them to etale local systems. Its equivalence also descends their quotient maps and normalization identities; these identities hold on the constant finite-module models. Use the adic fibre convention of [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors] there, taking finite-level etale fibres, inverse limit, and then inversion of $\varpi$. For the normalized lisse systems of $F$ and $N$, [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension](2) identifies the level-$n$ tensor fibre with $F_{n,\bar x}\otimes_{A_n}L_{n,\bar x}$, by the map sending tensor germs to the germ of their tensor. Those maps commute with reduction because the same pure-tensor formula holds at every $n$. By [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1),(2), the limits recover the finite $A$-modules of the two fibres. The second is finite free; after a basis choice tensor with it is a finite direct sum, so it commutes with the inverse limit and the displayed fibre becomes $F_{\bar x}\otimes_AN_{\bar x}$. This identification itself is basis independent: it is induced by the compatible tensor maps. Inverting $\varpi$ gives the desired $E$-fibre formula, and extending scalars gives the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ formula. This is a calculation of adic fibres, with the fibres on $X$ read from their lisse strata; it does not interchange the ordinary pro-etale stalk functor with an infinite inverse limit.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1); finite-level tensor fibres and complete finite-module limits, with the adic fibre convention stated in the item.

proof.text: At every level set $L_n^*=\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(L_n,(A_n)_X)$ on the etale site. Locally $L_n=A_n^r$, so $L_n^*=A_n^r$ with the dual basis, and finite-free duality gives $L_{n+1}^*\otimes_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong L_n^*$. These maps agree on overlaps: for a change-of-basis matrix $g$, the dual transition is $(g^{-1})^{\mathsf t}$, whose reduction is the inverse transpose of the reduction of $g$. Consequently they define a normalized finite-free system. By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] its inverse-limit realization is the locally free $B$-module $N^*=\mathcal Hom_B(N,B)$: reduction of this evaluation-defined identification is the identity dual-basis identification on each trivializing cover. Its membership in the integral category follows again from [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], with one stratum and local model $A^r[0]$. It defines a lisse $E$-sheaf and hence a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf. Taking finite-level fibres and limits as in Step 7 identifies its fibre with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(N_{\bar x},A)$; in a basis both sides are $A^r$ and evaluation is $\sum_i a_ib_i$. Inverting $\varpi$ identifies it with the $E$-linear dual, and then with the stated algebraic linear dual after extension.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3 and Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4); finite-free dual-basis and quotient calculation.

proof.text: Finally identify the derived internal dual. The functor $\mathcal Hom_B(N,-)$ is exact: restrict a short exact sequence to a trivializing slice using [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], then use [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact]; the local exact sequences imply global exactness by the sheaf axiom. The canonical restriction of ordinary sheaf Hom here follows its definition as maps on each slice, so it is compatible with these restrictions. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] with the one-term complex $N[0]$ to a K-injective resolution $B[0]\to I^\bullet$. It says that $N^*[0]=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_B(N[0],B[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_B(N[0],I^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The target computes $R\mathcal Hom_B(N,B)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Thus the coefficient derived dual is exactly $N^*[0]$, with its evaluation normalization. It is constructible by Step 8, so its rationalization is one of the pairs for which the rational internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is defined. Rationalization gives $\mathcal L^\vee\cong R\mathcal Hom_E(\mathcal L,E_X)$; the coefficient unit is the image of $B[0]$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tag 08JH, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect, specialized to a locally finite-free one-term complex.

proof.text: For $E\subset E'$ the comparisons for completed tensor and internal Hom, their naturality, and their identity and tower equations are supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. They apply to $K_A,N$ and the coefficient unit, which lie in the required integral categories by the preceding steps. Cohomology also commutes with this scalar extension: [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis] gives an $A$-basis of $A'=\mathcal O_{E'}$. Taking finite-quotient limits gives $B'_X\cong B_X^{\oplus[E':E]}$ as $B_X$-modules. Indeed the basis map on coefficients is a homeomorphism for their adic topologies: the ideals generated by powers of the two uniformizers are cofinal. In a basis, extension of scalars is a finite direct sum and commutes with kernels, images and quotients as in Step 4; hence it is t-exact and the cycles-and-boundaries comparison commutes with it. On fibres and duals, the maps are respectively $(v\otimes w)\otimes c\mapsto(v\otimes1)\otimes(w\otimes c)$ and $(\phi\otimes c)(v\otimes d)=cd\phi(v)$. These formulas agree with the finite-level balanced maps and dual evaluations already used. Their identity and associativity equations hold on pure tensors and hence on the whole modules. Therefore all cohomology, fibre and dual comparisons agree after any further finite extension. Every object, morphism and equality in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is represented at a common finite stage; the tower equations show that the comparisons descend independently of that stage. This proves all assertions over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, including naturality.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4; scalar-extension coherence as stated in the cited completed-operations lemma.
